sources.citation: Pepijn Brandon, “From Williams’s Thesis to Williams Thesis: An Anti-Colonial Trajectory,” International Review of Social History 62 (2017): 305–327. doi:10.1017/S0020859017000190.

verification.note: Fresh actual original Cambridge journal HTML and 23-leaf PDF retrieved. Selected 305–309,313–320 and 324–327 with associated notes read;318 and 325 visually checked. James’s concrete draft and chapter intervention, bibliographical resource and distinct criticism of the 1942 forecast are mediated through Brandon, Boodhoo, García Muñiz and the quoted original passages. Full original Williams 1938/1942/1944 and James books, drafts and review unread. Brandon’s nuanced Ragatz/Hochstetter antecedents and his explicit speculative limits on Marx retained; the proposed political reason for omitting Hochstetter is Brandon’s inference, not verified motive. Strong missing formation and named criticisms retained.

sources.scope_note: Named scholarly reconstruction of formation and disagreement; selected actual text, explicit original-reading limits.

williams_capitalism_primary.note: Fresh complete original preface dated 12 September 1943 read in a licensed UNC Press third-edition 2021 preview, retained original preview lines 1257–1275. Text distinguishes industrial finance from later abolition and identifies Ragatz, Pitman, Herskovits and Burch as manuscript readers with suggestions, Harlow as doctoral supervisor, and separate institutional, statistical and family assistance. Strong missing-endpoint scholarly helpers are held. Original 1944 print pages not visually collated, whole book and bibliography unread. Adjacent 2020 Darity foreword and 1994 Palmer introduction are distinct editorial voices; only selected adjoining paragraphs observed, no complete reading claimed.
